info.title: API.SH: Capitol Trades
info.description: The Capitol Trades API from API.SH: public Capitol Trades data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.summary: Fetch a past response again, free
get.description: The exact response a call returned, for 30 days after the call, at no cost. Use the call's x-request-id. Supports output=csv|ndjson.

200.description: The stored response (headers: x-refetch: 1, x-original-time, x-original-route).

404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

get.description:
One issuer: name, ticker, sector, country and state, last price, market cap, price change over 1 day, 7 days, 30 days, 90 days, 1 year and year to date, number of trades and politicians, traded volume, first and last trade dates, the buy/sell split, recent trades by politicians and related articles.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/capitoltrades-issuer

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Issuer id (e.g. 433770) or a capitoltrades.com/issuers/... link. Find ids with /capitoltrades/v1/issuer-search.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Find an issuer's id by company name or ticker: id, name, ticker, sector, country, state, trades, politicians, volume, last trade date, market cap, last price and price changes.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/capitoltrades-issuer-search

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Company name or ticker, at least 2 characters.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Companies and assets politicians trade: issuer id, name, ticker, sector, number of trades and politicians, traded volume, last trade date, last price and recent daily closes. Filter by name, sector, market cap band, country and state; sort by trades, politicians, last trade, volume or market cap. Pass `next_page` back as `page`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/capitoltrades-issuers

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Name search, e.g. `nvidia`.

parameters.name: sector
parameters.description: Sector(s), e.g. `energy` (same values as the trades filter).

parameters.name: mcap
parameters.description: Market cap band(s), 1-6.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Two-letter country code(s).

parameters.name: issuer_state
parameters.description: Two-letter US state code(s).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort: -countTrades, countTrades, -countPoliticians, countPoliticians, -dateLastTraded, dateLastTraded, -volume, volume, -mcap, mcap.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (default 1). Pass `next_page` back here; null on the last page.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Results per page, 1-100 (default 12).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
One politician: name, party, chamber, state, district, photo, trades, filings, issuers, traded volume, last trade date, years active, date of birth and age, official and social links, most traded issuers and sectors, the issuers traded with market cap, last price and price changes, recent trades (up to 100) and related articles. For every trade, page /capitoltrades/v1/trades with `politician`.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/capitoltrades-politician

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Politician id (e.g. P000197) or a capitoltrades.com/politicians/... link.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

Politicians who trade: id, name, party, state, photo, number of trades and issuers, traded volume and last trade date. Filter by name, party, chamber, state and committee; sort by last trade, trades, issuers, volume or name. Pass `next_page` back as `page`; null on the last page.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/capitoltrades-politicians

parameters.name: q

parameters.name: party

parameters.name: chamber

parameters.name: state

parameters.name: committee

parameters.name: sort

parameters.name: page

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Results per page, 1-100 (default 12).

get.description:
US congressional stock trades from members' periodic transaction reports: trade id and link, trade and publication dates, reporting delay in days, buy/sell/exchange/receive, owner (self, spouse, joint, child, undisclosed), estimated value and price, the politician (id, name, party, state, chamber, gender, date of birth) and the issuer (id, name, ticker, sector, country, state), with every filter the site offers. Up to 100 per page; `total` and `total_pages` give the full count. Pass `next_page` back as `page`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/capitoltrades-trades

parameters.name: politician
parameters.description: Politician id(s), comma separated, e.g. `P000197` (ids come from /capitoltrades/v1/politicians).

parameters.name: issuer
parameters.description: Issuer id(s), comma separated, e.g. `433770` (ids come from /capitoltrades/v1/issuer-search).

parameters.name: party
parameters.description: Party, comma separated: democrat, republican, other.

parameters.name: chamber
parameters.description: Chamber: house or senate.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Politician's state, two-letter code(s), e.g. `ca,ny`.

parameters.name: committee
parameters.description: Committee code(s), e.g. `hsag` (House Agriculture), `ssfi` (Senate Finance), `hsba` (House Financial Services).

parameters.name: asset_type
parameters.description: Asset type(s): stock, etf, crypto, mutual-fund, corporate-bond, municipal-security, stock-options, reit, abs, etn, futures, indices, preferred-shares, private-equity-fund, venture-capital, hedge-pvt-eq-funds-non-eif, non-public-stock, other-investment-fund, other-securities, ownership-interest, stock-appreciation-right, variable-annuity.

parameters.name: tx_type
parameters.description: Transaction type(s): buy, sell, exchange, receive.

parameters.name: mcap
parameters.description: Issuer market cap band(s), 1-6: 1 mega (over $200B), 2 large, 3 mid, 4 small, 5 micro, 6 nano (under $50M).

parameters.name: issuer_state
parameters.description: Issuer's US state, two-letter code(s).

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Issuer's country, two-letter code(s), e.g. `gb`.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: Label(s): faang, crypto, memestock, spac.

parameters.name: gender
parameters.description: Politician gender: male or female.

parameters.name: sector
parameters.description: Issuer sector(s): communication-services, consumer-discretionary, consumer-staples, energy, financials, health-care, industrials, information-technology, materials, real-estate, utilities, other.

parameters.name: tx_date
parameters.description: Trade date window: 30d, 90d, 180d, 365d, all (the site keeps about three years), or a range `2026-01-01,2026-03-31`.

parameters.name: pub_date
parameters.description: Publication date window, same values as tx_date.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort: -pubDate (default, newest published first), pubDate, -txDate, txDate, reportingGap, -reportingGap.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number (default 1). Pass `next_page` back here; null on the last page.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Results per page, 1-100 (default 12).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
